definition: The Afghan Girls Robotics Team, also known as the Afghan Dreamers, is an all-girl robotics team from Herat, Afghanistan, founded through the Digital Citizen Fund (DCF) in 2017 by Roya Mahboob and Alireza Mehraban.
details: It is made up of girls between ages 12 and 18 and their mentors. Several members of the team were relocated to Qatar and Mexico by humanitarian and tech entrepreneur Sarah Porter following the fall of Kabul in August 2021. A documentary film featuring members of the team, titled Afghan Dreamers, was released by MTV Documentary Films in 2023.

explainer.lead: The Afghan Girls Robotics Team is an all-girl robotics group from Herat, Afghanistan, that has built competition robots, low-cost medical ventilators, and disinfection robots—often while navigating war, visa denials, and the Taliban takeover of their country. Their story illustrates how STEM education can flourish in the most constrained environments and how quickly it can be uprooted.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a group of friends who love building things with LEGOs, but they live somewhere where girls aren't always allowed to learn tech stuff. They built robots in a basement using scrap metal, then traveled to other countries to compete against teams with fancy equipment. When things got dangerous at home, they had to leave everything behind—but they kept building robots anyway, now from places like Qatar and Mexico.
tiers.practitioner: The team operates as a competitive robotics organization using standard educational robotics platforms (FIRST Global Challenge, Robotex) with mentor-guided development cycles. Their 2020 ventilator project adapted an MIT open-source design, substituting locally available automotive parts (Toyota Corolla, Honda motorcycle chain) to reduce unit cost from ~$50,000 to ~$500. Key challenges include supply chain constraints, safety equipment scarcity, and geopolitical disruption of team continuity.
tiers.paperLevel: Not applicable—this is a human organization rather than a formal technical method. Their ventilator prototype (July 2020) was developed under guidance from MIT engineers and surgeon Douglas Chin, using a chain-drive mechanism and automotive components. No peer-reviewed publication is named in the sources.

explainer.mission: To develop girls' skills in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics through hands-on robotics projects and international competition, and to create pathways for women in STEM in Afghanistan.
explainer.founded: 2017 in Herat, Afghanistan, by Roya Mahboob and Alireza Mehraban through the Digital Citizen Fund (DCF), after Dean Kamen recruited Mahboob to form a team for the FIRST Global Challenge.
